item.title: Mansoor Delane was a full participant in Wednesday's practice
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Chiefs rookie corner Mansoor Delane is trending toward playing in the Week 2 matchup against the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs rookie corner Mansoor Delane is trending toward playing in the Week 2 matchup against the Colts.

Delane (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, according to the team's injury report.

Delane was able to play just three snaps before exiting Monday night's eventual victory over the Broncos. He registered an interception off Bo Nix on his third career snap.

Notably, defensive tackle Chris Jones (calf) was a limited participant to start the week.

Defensive back Chamarri Conner (knee) and left tackle Josh Simmons (back) did not participate.

Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (foot), receiver Rashee Rice (knee), cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee), defensive end R Mason Thomas (hamstring), and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) were all full participants.

item.title: Todd Monken: I wouldn't say Deshaun Watson is playing to earn start in Week 3
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Browns head coach Todd Monken stuck with Deshaun Watson as the team's starting quarterback for this week's game against the Buccaneers, but some are already looking ahead to what he'll do in Week 3.
item.content:encoded:
Browns head coach Todd Monken stuck with Deshaun Watson as the team's starting quarterback for this week's game against the Buccaneers, but some are already looking ahead to what he'll do in Week 3.

That will be the Browns' home opener and Watson's last appearance in Cleveland came amid cascades of boos during a preseason game. During a press conference on Wednesday, Monken was asked if Watson is in a position where he has to play well enough to earn another start.

"I wouldn't say that," Monken said. "I always expect our players to play well. I wouldn't put them out there if I didn't. I expect him to play really well and there were moments on Sunday when he did."

There were also moments when he didn't, of course, and it won't take too many more of those to guarantee a similar reaction to Watson taking the field in Cleveland to the same reaction he got this summer. Monken has shrugged off fan reaction to his decisions in the past, but there would seem to be a level Watson has to reach this Sunday in order for the Browns to continue trying to salvage something from his tenure with the team.

item.title: Steve Belichick resigns as North Carolina defensive coordinator
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Bill Belichick's son steps down amid an ongoing investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Two weeks after North Carolina G.M. Michael Lombardi abruptly resigned during an investigation regarding his conduct while working for the Tar Heels, North Carolina defensive coordinator Steve Belichick has done the same.

Via Pete Thamel of ESPN, Steve Belichick has resigned.

The son of head coach Bill Belichick, Steve has been on medical leave since August 6. No details regarding the medical condition were ever disclosed or reported.

On the day Lombardi resigned, WRAL issued a report that indicated the investigation has broadened to include Steve Belichick. Per the report, witnesses were being questioned regarding whether Steve Belichick “used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player.”

There was talk when Bill Belichick took the North Carolina job that he hoped to create a succession plan that would result in Steve Belichick taking over following Bill's retirement. The contracts did not contemplate the eventual shift, and the team's performance in 2025 seemingly mooted the possibility.

Now, it definitely won't happen. The only question is whether, and when, Bill Belichick will step down.

Through it all, UNC is 2-0. It nevertheless seems as if someone (or more than one someones) at UNC are looking for an exit strategy as to the relationship with Bill Belichick, possibly through a for-cause termination that cuts off his buyout.

item.title: Seahawks rule Sam Darnold out for Week 2
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The team does not plan to put Darnold on injured reserve.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks will not have Sam Darnold back in the lineup for Week 2.

Head coach Mike Macdonald said at his Wednesday press conference that Darnold has been ruled out for this week's game against the Cardinals. Drew Lock will start in Arizona on Sunday afternoon.

Darnold left last Wednesday's game against the Patriots in the first half with what was called a hip injury at the time and was later updated to a glute tendon issue. There was word that Darnold could miss a month or more due to the injury, but Macdonald said that the Seahawks do not plan to place him on injured reserve.

Macdonald also said that the Seahawks do not anticipate adding another quarterback to go with Lock or Jalen Milroe while Darnold is out of action.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Browns are adding a player who's plenty familiar with their (current) backup quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns are adding a player who's plenty familiar with their (current) backup quarterback.

According to multiple reports, Cleveland is signing receiver Jimmy Horn Jr. to its practice squad.

Horn — a Panthers sixth-round pick in last year's draft — had a rough Week 1, muffing a punt while trying to make a fair catch. He was waived earlier this week as the team added a linebacker.

Horn could help the Browns as a returner, as Dylan Sampson is expected to miss significant time with a knee injury suffered during the season-opening loss to the Jaguars.

Horn played with Shedeur Sanders at Colorado before both were drafted last year. With Deshaun Watson struggling through Cleveland's season opener as QB1, Sanders could be elevated to a starting role sooner than later.

item.title: Michael Penix: I'm dying to be out there, some goals I still have to achieve
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Falcons haven't named a starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Panthers and Michael Penix didn't do much to suggest that he'll be the choice during his Wednesday press conference.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons haven't named a starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Panthers and Michael Penix didn't do much to suggest that he'll be the choice during his Wednesday press conference.

Penix has been practicing for some time and said that he "felt good out there" during practice earlier in the day, but he was inactive last week and said he's "still working toward" feeling ready for game action. Penix is recovering from his third torn ACL and said that there are still some physical milestones he wants to reach before declaring himself all the way back.

“I’m close. I know I’ve been saying that, but there are there's a couple of technical things I want to hit, some goals that I have that I want to achieve before I do step foot out on that field. . . . Dying to be out there, but, at the same time, I gotta think about how I feel and think about things I need to work on and make sure I hit before I go out there," Penix said.

Penix stressed that the remaining steps are physical rather than mental and "whenever my knee feels good, I’m gonna be out there." He didn't rule out the possibility that could be this weekend, but he and the Falcons have taken the long view thus far and it seems hard to believe they'd speed things up at the very end.

item.title: Kyler Murray will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Murray is progressing through the concussion protocol after sustaining a hard hit on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
There’s some positive news on the injury front for Minnesota’s starting quarterback.

Kyler Murray is set to be a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, head coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters in his press conference.

Murray is in concussion protocol after taking a hard hit while sliding early on in Sunday’s victory over the Packers.

“We’ll see how he responds and continue to rely on the medical folks in that regard,” O’Connell said. “The good thing is the amount of reps he got from obviously competing and then being named the starter, he’s got a lot of reps logged away. But, yeah, really we’re taking it kind of period-by-period as far as the plan we have. But we want to be monitoring how he’s doing from a standpoint of that limited participation.

“It’s a little bit more of a vague thing at the quarterback position, just because they’re in red jerseys anyway all the way up until game time. So we’ll kind of just deal with it as it comes to us.”

Murray was on the field for just 11 offensive snaps before exiting the contest. Carson Wentz came in and played the rest of the way, completing 12-of-19 passes for 133 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.

Wentz would be in line to start on Sunday against the Bears if Murray does not clear the protocol.

item.title: Leonard Williams: "We all have faith" in Drew Lock
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Seahawks believe in Sam Darnold's replacement.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks will ride with quarterback Drew Lock until Sam Darnold returns from a glute injury. And Lock's teammates have no problem with that.

"[W]e all have faith in Drew," defensive lineman Leonard Williams told reporters on Wednesday. "We believe that he’s the best second-string quarterback in the league. Since I’ve been here, before he went to the Giants, he stepped up big time. I remember that Eagles game a few years back where he stepped up and won us the game. He’s done it and shown it multiple times now. That has instilled a lot of trust in his teammates and his team.”

After three years with the Broncos, Lock spent two in Seattle. He signed with the Giants for 2024 before returning to the Seahawks in 2025.

And Lock did indeed have a special night against the Eagles in December 2023. Starting in place of Geno Smith, Lock threw a touchdown pass to receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 28 seconds to play for a 20-17 win over Philly.

“He has a little bit of swagger to him," Williams said regarding Lock. "He’s confident, he’s ready for the moment. When it’s time for him to be called up, there’s no lag, there’s no hesitation. He’s ready for it. It’s cool to see because I can’t imagine what it’s like to be in that position as a backup quarterback. You may not see the field all season but at any moment you have to be ready to go in there and operate and lead the offense. He does a great job of that, not skipping a beat.”

This week, Lock knows he'll be playing against the Cardinals. The duration of his assignment remains to be seen.

item.title: Kyrie Irving offers to pay Azeez Al-Shaair's fine
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL has fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for having a personal message written on his black eye strips during the Week 1 game against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for having a personal message written on his black eye strips during the Week 1 game against the Bills. Mavericks star Kyrie Irving has Al-Shaair covered.

"I’ll take care of his fine," Irving said on social media, via ESPN.

Al-Shaair, who was fined in January for wearing "stop the genocide" on his eye-black strips, played Sunday's game with the name "Hind Rajab" written in the space. The five-year-old girl was killed by Israeli forces, along with six members of her family, when their car came under fire in Gaza City in 2024.

The league generally prohibits any personal messaging without prior approval.

The league also prohibits the payment of fines by anyone other than the person being fined. But that can't stop Irving from giving Al-Shaair a gift in the amount of, say, $11,941, if Irving so chooses.

And while Al-Shaair is doing well enough to pay the fine on his own, with a contract that pays out on average $18 million per year, Irving is making nearly $40 million in 2026-27.

The next question is whether Al-Shaair will try to do it again in Week 2 against the Bengals, and whether he'll be prevented from playing. After he was fined for having the message on his eye black during the wild-card win at Pittsburgh, Al-Shaair was told he'd not be permitted to play in the divisional round at New England if he tried to do it again.

item.content:encoded:
Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush revealed an interesting note about Wednesday's practice during his press conference following the session.

Rush said he and Michael Penix Jr. split the first-team reps at QB to start the practice week.

"I don’t know exactly the amount. But we were both out there, me and Mike," Rush said. "It was good work."

Rush started for the Falcons in their Week 1 loss to the Steelers. Atlanta has not yet publicly determined who will start for the club against Carolina this week.

Penix may be splitting reps, but it’s not clear whether or not he’ll be fully ready to play a game on Sunday.

Rush finished the Week 1 loss 12-of-22 for 143 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. He took four sacks.

item.description: The Vikings will not have one of their key contributors at running back for at least the next four weeks.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings will not have one of their key contributors at running back for at least the next four weeks.

Head coach Kevin O’Connell said in his Wednesday press conference that Jordan Mason is being placed on injured reserve due to a thumb fracture.

O’Connell noted Mason has already undergone a procedure to repair the injury and the team does not anticipate him being out longer than the four-week IR window.

Mason had 59 yards on 15 carries with a touchdown in the season-opening victory over the Packers.

As a corresponding move, the team is signing DeeJay Dallas to the 53-man roster off of its practice squad.

Additionally, veteran back Jerome Ford has been signed to the practice squad.

item.title: Joe Burrow dealing with back tightness, expects to play against Texans
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will be on this week's injury report, but he doesn't expect to be at risk of missing Sunday's game against the Texans.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will be on this week's injury report, but he doesn't expect to be at risk of missing Sunday's game against the Texans.

Reporters at the open portion of the team's practice on Wednesday noted that Burrow was not doing much work and Burrow said at a post-practice press conference that he is dealing with back tightness. Burrow said he didn't know if there was a specific play from last Sunday's win over the Buccaneers that led to the issue because he did not start feeling anything until after the game.

Burrow said he is unsure if he'll be able to practice for the rest of the week, but called it "ridiculous" to think he'd need to miss Sunday's game in order to avoid making the problem any worse. Burrow also expressed confidence that he can get enough "mental reps" to be ready for Houston even if he doesn't fully participate in practice.

Joe Flacco is the backup quarterback in Cincinnati, but it doesn't sound like there's any thought being given to the possibility of playing him in Houston.

item.title: Dave Canales on not knowing Falcons QB: Have to study history of Kevin Stefanski's offenses
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Falcons have not named a quarterback for Sunday's game against the Panthers and preparing the team's defense under those circumstances was a topic of conversation for Panthers head coach Dave Canales on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons have not named a quarterback for Sunday's game against the Panthers and preparing the team's defense under those circumstances was a topic of conversation for Panthers head coach Dave Canales on Wednesday.

Cooper Rush started for Atlanta last week with Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix inactive, but Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has not committed to giving him a second start. Tagovailoa did not practice Wednesday and Penix said he still has milestones he wants to reach in his recovery from last season's torn ACL, but Penix did not rule out getting there by Sunday.

Canales said the team will focus on Stefanski's own history because there isn't a major difference in playing styles between the quarterbacks.

"We just have to look at the history of Kevin Stefanski's offenses and what he values and what he's trying to get done. . . . The good part is no singular quarterback that they have is kind of a standout in terms of being a runner," Canales said, via the team's website. "Where when you have pocket passers, and these are all quarterbacks that I think are good quarterbacks, and, certainly, Tua, we've seen Michael Penix play at his best, and Cooper Rush, who's been around a long time. So these are guys that can really operate. As a former quarterbacks coach, I value what they can do. There isn't a dynamic of the zone-read type of element, a guy that kind of creates that extra special element. So we can really treat the system and the offense true to the integrity of what Coach Stefanski is trying to get done."

Whatever choice the Falcons make, the Panthers defense will need to be a lot stronger than they were while being strafed by the Bears in a 59-37 loss in Week 1.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer: I don't worry about George Pickens's drops, he'll be just fine
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Among the reasons why the Cowboys lost 28-20 to the Giants in Week 1 were a pair of dropped passes by wide receiver George Pickens.
item.content:encoded:
Among the reasons why the Cowboys lost 28-20 to the Giants in Week 1 were a pair of dropped passes by wide receiver George Pickens.

Both drops came in the first half and the second came just before halftime on a pass that would have helped put the Cowboys in position to break a 7-7 tie. Dak Prescott threw an interception a few plays later and the Giants turned that into a 14-7 lead at the break.

On Wednesday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked whether he talked to Pickens about the plays. Schottenheimer said he didn't feel the need to because it was uncharacteristic of the wideout's usual efforts.

“I don’t say anything to George. George will be just fine," Schottenheimer said. "He’s gonna usually catch that ball going down the sideline and probably pull through it, then jump over people and spin and then jump into the end zone. So, I don't worry about George."

Pickens said he understands the need to button things up ahead of this week's game against the Commanders.

"It's definitely urgent, because it's [another] division game, such as the Giants was," Pickens said, via the team's website. "We definitely need to nail down our Ps and Qs. I think that's the mindset that people are honing in now."

Pickens can't help with a defense that underwhelmed against the Giants, but holding onto the ball could lead to more points that makes the job easier for players on that side of the ball.

item.content:encoded:
Texans wide receiver Nico Collins was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury that took place during the session.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Collins picked up the injury during the workout. He went for further evaluation after practice was over and doctors believe that he avoided a serious injury.

That doesn't put Collins in the clear for this Sunday's game against the Bengals, however. Hamstring injuries can linger and playing before an issue is resolved can sometimes aggravate the initial injury.

More word on Collins's status will come with Thursday's injury report, but a final decision on his availability in Week 2 may go down to the wire.

item.title: Caleb Williams preparing for "mental war" with Brian Flores this weekend
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams wants the team to score points every time they have the ball and they came close to doing that against the Panthers in Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams wants the team to score points every time they have the ball and they came close to doing that against the Panthers in Week 1.

Things could be a bit tougher this week. The Bears will be hosting the Vikings and their defensive coordinator Brian Flores can make things very difficult on opposing quarterbacks. Flores can deploy a heavy load of blitzes — he sent extra rushers nearly 80 percent of the time in last Sunday's win over Green Bay — or he can show pressure only to dial it back at the snap in an effort to confuse quarterbacks.

Williams has had mixed success against the Vikings in the past and called preparing to face a Flores-led defense a "big challenge" in his Wednesday press conference.

“It’s a game-plan defense. He’s gonna game plan from first snap to last snap," Williams said. "Coach calls this 'mental war' when you go against versus him. That's what it is. You've got to be able to go out there bad things are going to happen, bad things are gonna happen. You've got to be able to fight back and stay steady. That's one of the biggest things is not allowing his defense and all of that to fluster you and get in your mind. That’s one of the first. You stay steady and now it's time to go make plays and get completions and when the big ones show up, take them and find them."

Solving whatever Flores throws his way this weekend will be crucial to the Bears' chances of winning the game and it would show Williams's continued development as a quarterback who can find ways to succeed in every situation that comes his way. The latter victory wouldn't count in the standings immediately, but it would have a positive impact on that front over the long run.

item.title: Travis Kelce knows he was holding on Patrick Mahomes' touchdown run
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Kelce held Denver's Talanoa Hufanga, but the officials didn't see it.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce got away with a hold on Patrick Mahomes' 15-yard touchdown run on Monday night.

Kelce acknowledged on his New Heights podcast that he could have been called for holding Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga on the play, which gave the Chiefs a 7-0 lead in a game they would go on to win 31-10.

“It was definitely a questionable play," Kelce said. "That’s one of those where you get up slowly like, ‘Please don’t be any laundry on the field.' I had the man up by his neck Can’t do it. Can’t do it. Almost cost us. That would've been Patrick Mahomes' second rushing touchdown called back in two plays, it was the same thing. That would've taken us out of the red zone. That was risky business. You know what? Sometimes you're just living right."

Kelce's hold was shown on the TV broadcast, but none of the officials on the field had a good view of it, and holding isn't reviewable on replay. Kelce got away with one.

item.title: Report: Keenan Allen's BAC was measured at 0.224 percent
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Colts receiver Keenan Allen faces an enhanced misdemeanor charge for DUI, because his blood-alcohol concentration (alcohol concentration equivalent, in Indiana parlance) exceeded 0.15 percent after he was arrested last month.
item.content:encoded:
Colts receiver Keenan Allen faces an enhanced misdemeanor charge for DUI, because his blood-alcohol concentration (alcohol concentration equivalent, in Indiana parlance) exceeded 0.15 percent after he was arrested last month.

Allen's BAC didn't exceed 0.15 percent by just a little bit.

Via Stephen Holder of ESPN, the number measured following Allen's arrest was 0.224 percent. That's significantly beyond the legal limit of 0.08 percent.

The number came from a breath test. Allen also gave a blood sample. That result has not yet been released.

If the measurement is accurate, Allen was extremely intoxicated — approaching potential alcohol poisoning. Under the NFL's substance-abuse policy, Allen is subject to something more than a three-game suspension.

From the policy: "If the Commissioner finds that there were aggravating circumstances, including but not limited to felonious conduct, extreme intoxication (BAC of .15% or more), property damage or serious injury or death to the Player or a third party, and/or if the Player has had prior drug or alcohol-related misconduct, increased discipline may be imposed."

The timeline for the resolution of Allen's case isn't known. He could possibly get through the current season without league-imposed punishment. And, if he retires after the 2026 season, he'll ultimately face no league discipline at all.

item.title: A new book, Accessory After The Fact, is coming
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: During the first year of the pandemic, after the draft ended and the NFL basically shut down, I had more free time than I'd had in years.
item.content:encoded:
During the first year of the pandemic, after the draft ended and the NFL basically shut down, I had more free time than I'd had in years. So I started writing something other than the usual stream of NFL updates and analysis and whatever else landed on the PFT radar screen.

After I finished Father of Mine (the ebook is a mere 99 cents), I started on the sequel, Son of Mine (also 99 cents). When that one was finished, I started another. Then another. And another.

After doing the traditional publisher thing with Playmakers (nonfiction, but some would say it's fiction in parts), I wanted to control everything about the process — the content, the cover, all of it. It's now time to try a different approach.

The latest one, Accessory After The Fact, will be published next summer by Crooked Lane Books. It's about a pro football player who goes to law school after his career ends, gets a job in a Pittsburgh firm, finds a former teammate who escaped from prison hiding in his house after the first day of work, and gets assigned to assist with a high-profile murder case the next morning.

It's potentially the first book in a series, depending on whether anyone, you know, buys the first one. And there are seven or eight other books (I've lost count) that are generally ready to go.

Hopefully, one of the manuscripts already in the hopper will be the second in the two-book deal with Crooked Lane. If not, I'll have to write another one. Because I will anyway. Finish one, start the next. Finish that one, start the next. After nearly a quarter century of updating PFT every single day, I can think fast and type fast and crank out a couple of books per year. (My wife has suggested that I spend a little more time focusing on quality, not quantity.)

You'll be hearing more about Accessory After The Fact in the coming weeks. It will eventually be available for preorder, and I'll come up with other ways to persuade you to give it a try.

Until then, Father of Mine, Son of Mine, On Our Way Home, and Big Shield are available in ebook form for less than a buck (or at no extra charge if you've subscribed to Kindle Unlimited).

I've also got another potential surprise in the hopper, which may coincide with the upcoming 25-year anniversary of the launch of PFT. That one will be completely and totally free, if I can figure out how to effectively pull it off.

For now, set aside some reading time next summer for Accessory After The Fact. It's good. My editor at Crooked Lane, Sara Henry, has already made it a lot better. By the time it comes out, it should be in the best shape possible.

item.title: NFLPA will "explore all options" regarding league's position on Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavien Harris
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After LSU slammed the door on former NFL tryout players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavien Harris, the NFL re-slammed the door on their potential return to pro football during the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
After LSU slammed the door on former NFL tryout players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavien Harris, the NFL re-slammed the door on their potential return to pro football during the 2026 season.

The situation leaves the two players caught in the middle, as men without options for 2026.

That may not be the end of it. Via Amanda Christovich of Front Office Sports, an NFLPA spokesperson said this: “We are aware of the memo and are in touch with each of the players' representatives. We will explore all options to ensure each player's rights are protected within the Collective Bargaining Agreement.”

Similarly, agent Drew Rosenhaus (who represents Wright) told Christovich that Wright is considering his legal options based on the NFL's position that Wright and Harris can't return to the NFL, even though they never returned to college football.

The players union could, and perhaps should, file a grievance. The situation is unique, and the NFL seemingly created a rule on the fly, with no precedent to guide the decision — and apparently without a clear agreement from the NFLPA.

Wright and Harris have gotten the short end of the stick. They made a business decision to seek another year of college football after not making 53-man NFL rosters, and they secured the legal right to return to LSU for another season. But for the SEC's placement of extreme pressure on LSU, they'd both potentially be on the team.

With LSU blinking, Wright and Harris are left out in the cold with no college landing spot and, based on the NFL's position, no way to seek employment at the pro level.

item.title: ManningCast slumps to 705,000 viewers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Few TV shows have a more dramatic disconnect between industry and viewer response than the ManningCast.
item.content:encoded:
Few TV shows have a more dramatic disconnect between industry and viewer response than the ManningCast. The Peyton and Eli Show, an alternate Monday Night Football broadcast that will be televised 11 times during the regular season and the Super Bowl, continues to draw rave reviews from the critics — while not moving the needle that truly matters.

On Monday night, for example, only 705,000 of the 23.2 million viewers who watched the Broncos-Chiefs game were tuned in to ESPN2 for the combination football broadcast/talk show, via Andrew Marchand of The Athletic.

That's only three pecent of the total audience.

This year, the stakes become even higher, given that ESPN reportedly plans to have a Pat McAfee alternate broadcast on ESPN2 during the weeks that the Mannings don't do their show. What if the McAfee show outperforms the ManningCast?

The ultimate apples-to-apple comparison will happen during the Super Bowl, if the primary broadcast is accompanied by both a ManningCast and a McAfeeFest.

Everyone involved will say all the right things. They're teammates. The numbers don't matter. Yada. Yada. Yada. And they'll all obsess over the numbers, with whoever draws the smaller crowd becoming tormented by the final verdict, as issued by those who control the remote. Control.

item.title: NCAA's FBS Oversight Committee finds replay error marred Western Michigan-Michigan game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Western Michigan got hosed during their season-opening game against Michigan, and everyone knows it.
item.content:encoded:
Western Michigan got hosed during their season-opening game against Michigan, and everyone knows it.

The NCAA's FBS Oversight Committee knows it, too.

Via Nick Bromberg of Yahoo Sports, the NCAA released a statement on Wednesday acknowledging that the replay process reached the wrong result.

"The committee consulted with national officiating leadership regarding the instant replay protocols," the statement explained. "Based on that information, the committee agreed that the instant replay protocols were not followed in the contest's second-to-last play. Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different."

However, the committee also said that the rules prevent an appeal of the outcome of any game, once the game is declared to be ended.

While the statement won't change the official outcome, it reinforces the unofficial belief that Western Michigan won the game. Because Western Michigan did win the game.

item.title: Broncos-Chiefs drew 23.2 million viewers on Monday night
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Monday Night Football opener drew a big audience, with the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos getting 23.2 million viewers.
item.content:encoded:
The Monday Night Football opener drew a big audience, with the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos getting 23.2 million viewers.

That number includes everyone who watched the main broadcast on ESPN and ABC, the ManningCast on ESPN2, the Spanish broadcast on ESPN Deportes and the stream on NFL+. ESPN did not announce how many viewers watched on each platform that showed the game.

It was ESPN's most-watched Monday Night Football Week 1 game and third-most watched Monday night game ever, although historical comparisons can be misleading because ratings today count out-of-home viewers who previously weren't counted.

This year's audience was 5 percent greater than last year's Week 1 Monday Night Football audience, which was 22.1 million viewers.

The pregame show Monday Night Countdown, had 1.9 million viewers, a 7 percent increase over Week 1 last year. That's a fairly small increase given that Monday Night Countdown now airs on both NFL Network and ESPN.

item.title: Ken Zampese: Browns "mucked it up" with Baker Mayfield
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eight years to the day after Baker Mayfield made his debut for the Browns, he'll be facing the Browns in his fourth year as the starting quarterback of the Buccaneers.
item.content:encoded:
Eight years to the day after Baker Mayfield made his debut for the Browns, he'll be facing the Browns in his fourth year as the starting quarterback of the Buccaneers.

Buccaneers senior offensive assistant/pass game specialist Ken Zampese was Mayfield's position coach when he came off the bench to beat the Jets on September 20, 2018. And Zampese had some candid comments on Wednesday about how the Browns blew it with Baker.

"They had the guy," Zampese said, via Jenna Laine of ESPN. "They had the guy and they gave him up."

They gave him up once they decided to make a franchise-altering (in a bad way) trade for Deshaun Watson. Mayfield was later traded to the Panthers.

"The year we were there, we were one of the best offenses in the NFL the second half of that season, 5-3, in a place that was -- before that season started -- 1-31," Zampese said regarding Mayfield. "The script got flipped and the city came alive because they finally drafted a quarterback that worked out for them and they mucked it up. They mucked it up."

Zampese was reunited with Mayfield this year, continuing their relationship that went well in the one year when they worked together.

Mayfield, in his third season, led the Browns to a playoff appearance, a win over the Steelers in the wild-card round, and a near-miss against the Chiefs in the divisional round. After an injury-riddled 2021, the Browns made the decision to move on.

Does Zampese think the Browns believe they "mucked it up" with Mayfield?

"I don't know," Zampese said. "It doesn't matter. We got the guy we wanted [in Tampa] and that's what's important."

They'll have him on Sunday against the Browns. And the Bucs will be hoping to get the win that eluded them in Cincinnati to start the season.

item.title: Macklemore, Robert Kraft make significant donations to Palestinian relief
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The recent spat between Macklemore and Patriots owner Robert Kraft regarding Macklemore's presence on Ed Sheeran's tour has led to some good.
item.content:encoded:
The recent spat between Macklemore and Patriots owner Robert Kraft regarding Macklemore's presence on Ed Sheeran's tour has led to some good.

On Wednesday, Macklemore announced that he will be donating $1 million to Palestinian relief organizations.

“Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protection,” Macklemore wrote on social media. “A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any life on this earth."

Macklemore "invited" Kraft to match the donation. Kraft did, and he doubled it.

"Earlier today," Kraft said, "before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis. Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges."

Macklemore's exit from the tour happened after support for Palestine that Kraft believed "crossed the line" into hate speech. Other venues expressed concern, leading to Macklemore's exit from Sheeran's tour.

Regardless of the geopolitical forces at play, the simple fact remains that many human beings who simply hope to live their lives and love their families have been caught in the middle of hostilities for which they have no responsibility and in which they have no role. They need help, and they'll be getting more of it through these donations.

And perhaps the gestures will inspire others to donate to efforts to provide relief for those affected by the situation.

item.title: Hall of Fame moves on from 19 selectors
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Earlier this month, on the Friday before Labor Day weekend, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced a significant overhaul to the selection process, which was undoubtedly sparked by the inexplicable failure of Bill Belichick to secure enshrinement in his first year of eligibility.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this month, on the Friday before Labor Day weekend, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced a significant overhaul to the selection process, which was undoubtedly sparked by the inexplicable failure of Bill Belichick to secure enshrinement in his first year of eligibility.

Among the changes, the Hall of Fame said it will reduce the panel of voters from 50 to 28. (Of the 28, 25 will be voters and three will be non-voting participants.)

The Hall of Fame said that the new group of voters would be announced after the 50 existing members were informed of their status.

Many of them have been informed. Paul Kuharsky (one of the 50 who won't be returning) has posted a list of 19 voters who will not be voting on the 2027 class.

Removed from the panel, in addition to Kuharsky, were Rick Gosselin, Frank Cooney, John McClain, Tony Grossi, Ron Borges, Darin Gantt, Clark Judge, Geoff Hobson, Jason Cole, Armando Salguero, Mary Kay Cabot, Matt Maiocco, Tony Dungy, Bill Polian, Lisa Salters, Joel Bussert, Paul Gutierrez, and Rich Cimini.

As Kuharsky notes, the 19 departures account for 280 combined years of experience as Hall of Fame voters.

Kuharsky lists nine persons who will return: Charean Williams, Calvin Watkins, Jim Trotter, Jeff Legwold, Ira Kaufman, Howard Balzer, Gary Myers, Vahe Gregorian, and Mike Sando.

Gregorian made waves by disclosing that he didn’t vote for Belichick, opting instead to give the senior player candidates the opportunity to make it through in what likely was their last chance to do so.

There are 16 spots still to be determined, along with the three non-voting members.

It's unclear why or how fewer voters will make the process better. Frankly, it's unclear how any of the changes will improve the imperfect process of determining who does and who doesn't get a bronze bust in Canton.

UPDATE 6:42 p.m. ET: Kuharsky has added four more names to the group that has been dropped from the panel. They are Kent Somers, Alex Marvez, Gerry Dulac, and D. Orlando Ledbetter.
